title: Lighter Peruvian Lomo Saltado with Oven Fries
hook: Saturday steak night, Peruvian style: lomo saltado in 30 minutes, with oven fries
benefit: High in protein and iron, with oven fries instead of fried
ingredients: 1 lb lean sirloin or flank steak, sliced into thin 1/2-inch strips
1 1/2 lb Yukon gold potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch fries
1 large red onion, cut into thick wedges
1 tbsp aji amarillo paste (or 1 jalapeno, thinly sliced)
1/4 cup low-sodium beef or chicken broth
3 cups cooked brown rice, to serve
key_ingredients: 1/2 cup cilantro, brown rice to serve
steps: Heat the oven to 450F. Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp oil and 1/2 tsp salt on a lined sheet pan in one layer. Roast 25 to 30 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp.
Pat the steak dry and season with the cumin, pepper and remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Stir the soy sauce, vinegar and broth in a small bowl.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until it just smokes. Sear the steak in two batches, 1 to 2 minutes each, until browned but still pink inside. Move to a plate.
Stir-fry the onion 2 minutes until the edges char. Add the garlic and aji amarillo for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes for 1 minute, so they soften but hold their shape.
Return the steak and its juices, pour in the sauce and toss 1 minute until it bubbles and coats everything. Off the heat, fold in the cilantro and half the fries.
Serve over the brown rice with the rest of the fries on top and lime wedges to squeeze over. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge.
vo_steps: Oven to four fifty. Roast the fries twenty five to thirty minutes.
Season the steak with cumin, salt and pepper. Mix soy, vinegar and broth.
Sear the steak in a smoking hot pan, one to two minutes a batch.
Onion two minutes, then garlic and aji amarillo, then tomatoes one minute.
Steak back in with the sauce, toss one minute. Fold in cilantro and half the fries.
Serve over brown rice with the rest of the fries and a squeeze of lime.
